claims.summary: Column dichotomy for unary PHP^{n+1}_n on any bipartite graph G, any prime p: for a hole set H_0 with |H_0| >= n/2, if the systems {occupancy(h) = 1 mod p for h in H'}, over uniform r_0-subsets H' of H_0, hold with average probability at most delta, then for every eta in (0,1) a linear decision tree over F_p of depth O(r_0 log(2/eta)(log n + log(2/eta))) finds a falsified hole clause with probability at least 1 - 4 delta/3 - eta; boards without a matching covering n/2 holes are easy outright. So the closure method's probability property, if it charges these safe column systems, contradicts its distributional search hardness for every distribution on every board. Exempting the occupancy forms as Byramji-Impagliazzo Lemma 5.7 exempts column sums is blocked by safety: beside the n-p+1 fixed occupancy forms of the modular-collision distribution, a safe system has at most p further independent forms.

claims.summary: For unary PHP over F_p, p odd, the rank-one system x_{1a}+x_{2a}+x_{3a} = 2 (with occupancy equations, a having at least p further neighbours) forces a collision in hole a without forcing any cell, so closures defined by forced cells (one-shot, or iterated with matching propagation) fail the Efremenko-Garlik-Itsykson Delayer step at rank at most two. Any local-consistency notion requiring a 0/1 solution, monotone under implication over 0/1 points, with the leaf property and the Delayer step below rank m, must reject every system on m cells whose 0/1 solutions all collide there; for p >= 5 one equation can spread such collisions over p-2 holes, so a closure seeing them needs at least p-2 rows and holes.

claims.summary: Two closures for plain unary PHP over F_p fail the Delayer step on the full board. Private holes: with k = ceil(theta) and 2k+p <= n, Phi = {x_{i h_i} = 1 (i <= k), sum_i x_{j_i h_i} = 1} has a collision in every 0/1 solution, yet the vertex-cover closure (with or without the occupancy quotient) accepts it with witness the rows 1..k, since a closure pigeon's hole may hold other pigeons; by the rejection argument some query on a locally consistent system of rank at most 2k has no locally consistent answer, for every budget >= k and every theta > 1 in range. Row sums: a closure by matching edges (each closure pigeon in exactly one hole) accepts {sum_{i in R} row_i = v} with |R| = ceil(theta), v != |R| mod p, n >= max(2|R|, p), but no answer to row_{i_1} is locally consistent (rank two).

claims.summary: Over F_p, let Psi be affine equations in the cells of a bipartite graph between pigeons and holes in which every hole has a neighbour, W the span of the column forms and O' = {col_h = 1}. If Psi together with O' is consistent over F_p and <Psi> is theta-safe modulo W (least cover number of a representative at least theta times the quotient dimension), with theta >= l_q for the quotient rank q (the Alon-Linial-Meshulam number: (1-1/p)^(l-p+2) q < 1), then for every map d choosing a neighbour d(h) of each hole there is a 0/1 solution of Psi and O' with exactly one pigeon in every hole, equal to d(h) for all but at most l_q q holes. Proof: Edmonds' matroid intersection of the l_q-fold union of the switch-vector matroid with the column partition matroid, safety bounding the number of non-constant columns, then ALM Proposition 3.1.

claims.summary: Star closure for plain unary PHP on the full board over F_p (danger modulo the occupancy span, occupancy equations imposed): a witness is a set of closure pigeons, closure holes and an owner map, not necessarily onto; its pattern puts each closure pigeon exactly in its owned holes and each closure hole's only pigeon is its owner. With theta > 1: negated hole clauses are not locally consistent; negated pigeon clauses are (a closure pigeon may own nothing), but no system of rank below n/(p-1) with a 0/1 solution implies one (Olson). With theta >= l_r and rank at most r: locally consistent systems have a 0/1 solution with one pigeon per hole, and the Delayer step holds in one-node form: extending the closure greedily by the stars of a solution from lem:Fp-safe-forms-one-pigeon-per-hole gives alpha and sigma* with |sigma*| + 3 theta D* <= |sigma| + 3 theta (D+1) + l_r D. Along a single path the Delayer can keep one near-matching and the closure is at most 2 theta T after T queries, so the content is the one-node form.

claims.summary: For the modular-collision near-bijection mu_E on unary PHP over F_p (p >= 3: n+1 pigeons onto the holes outside a fixed set E of p-1 holes, one hole h* receiving p+1 pigeons): queries constant on the support are exactly those additive on pigeons x (holes outside E); (1) if the cells are partitioned among k players, integer sums of hole labels give an O(k log n)-bit protocol finding two colliding pigeons, so communication bounds through simulations where players hold cells give at most d = O(log n / log p) for linear trees (lifted simulations are not covered); (2) K = O(log n) fixed rank-one queries separate every support point from each of its single swaps (p >= 3), so single-swap sensitivity arguments give at most O(log n). claims.summary: Two simulation lemmas for unary queries over F_p. L1 (easy direction of the standard four-point test): if a matrix C is at distance dist(C) from additive matrices a_i + b_h, a random swap of two pigeons' holes changes Q_C = sum_i C(i, g(i)) with probability at least dist(C), for independent or bijective choices and, under mu_E, at least (1 - O(p^2/m^2)) dist(C). L2: for independent uniform bits and nonzero differences delta_k in F_p, |Pr[sum delta_k beta_k = v] - 1/p| <= ((p-1)/p) cos(pi/p)^t <= exp(-pi^2 t / (2 p^2)); if every delta_k = +-1 (rectangle queries) the maximal deviation is at least (sqrt 2 / p) cos(pi/p)^t, so about p^2 log(1/eta) swaps are needed; one swap gives only two values, so Byramji-Impagliazzo's one-bit localization does not transfer to odd p.

claims.summary: The marginal-bounds lemma: let G be a bipartite graph between pigeons A and holes B, |A| = |B| + p, in which every pigeon misses at most mu holes and every hole misses at most mu' pigeons, and nu_G the uniform law on maps g into G with one hole h* receiving p+1 pigeons (the set S*) and every other hole one. With b = |B| and F_1 = b - mu - mu' - 1: nu_G(g(i)=h, h regular) <= 1/F_1; nu_G(i in S*) <= (p+1)/F_1; nu_G(i, i' both in S*) <= p(p+1)/F_1^2; nu_G(h* = h) <= p! b^p / ((b-1) F_2^p) with F_2 = F_1 - p; and nu_G(g(i)=h, h regular) >= F_3 (1 - theta)/((b-1)(b-2)) for every edge, with F_3 = F_1 - 2 and theta = (2p+3)/F_1 + p! b^p/((b-1)F_2^p), hence pair marginals of order 1/b^2.

claims.summary: The graph swap-test lemma: if every pigeon misses fewer than |B|/3 holes of a bipartite graph G, every function C on the edges at distance dist from the additive functions a_i + b_h has alternating sum nonzero on at least a fraction dist/K of the 4-cycles of G, with K = (b(a-1)/((a-mu')(b-mu)))(1 + 3b/(b-3mu))(b/(b-2mu))^2 (K <= 7.3 when mu <= b/15, mu' <= a/15); in particular 4-cycle-invariant functions are additive. Example H: on the blow-up of the 6-cycle (each vertex adjacent to two of three classes) the function 1 on A_1 x B_2 is invisible to every 4-cycle, not additive, and its query is not constant on the support of nu_G (finite check: all values mod 3). Under nu_G with missing bounds <= b/15, a uniform pair of pigeons gives a detecting swap with probability at least dist/15.

claims.summary: The modular-collision theorem: for every odd prime p there are C_p, n_p such that for n >= n_p every linear decision tree over F_p (arbitrary affine queries in the variables x_{ih} of unary PHP with n+1 pigeons and n holes) of depth d that outputs two pigeons outputs two pigeons of one hole under the modular-collision near-bijection mu_E (n+1 pigeons onto the holes outside a fixed set E of p-1 holes, one hole receiving p+1) with probability at most C_p d sqrt((d + ln n)/n); so depth Omega_p(n^{1/3}) is needed for success probability 1/2. Proof: swap simulation in dense graphs; combinations of queries close to additive are made additive by revealing the pigeons on their exceptional cells, the others are localized on fresh random pairs whose orientations are hidden uniform bits (Fourier bound for systems), with a transfer from the prior along fixed paths to the adaptive tree.

claims.summary: The detecting-swaps lemma: for a dense class (fixed pigeons sent to distinct holes of H', and a remaining graph G' between A' and B' = H' minus those holes, |A'| = |B'| + p, such that G' and every G'-i-h satisfy the hypotheses of lem:near-bijection-dense-marginals with F_3 > 0 and theta < 1, every pigeon missing fewer than |B'|/3 holes; the class is all maps extending the fixed pigeons with the rest in the support of nu_{G'}): if L = a holds on the class, the coefficient matrix of L is additive on G'; if L != a holds on the class, no map has p-1 pairwise disjoint swaps changing L, and in the regime of the modular-collision theorem L is within 4(p-2)K_0/|A'| of additive on G' (K_0 <= 15). Hence, in that regime, a class implying an equation or inequation at distance eps from additive on the full board fixes at least eps m/4 pigeons or deletes about eps n m/2 cells.

claims.summary: The bounded-degree head-count lemma: let delta >= 2 and k <= s/4 and let H be q distinct subsets of [s] of sizes 1..delta (heads); with E the delta-sets containing a head and theta = |E|/C(s,delta) (theta >= q/(2^delta C(s,delta)), equality without 2^delta for delta-uniform heads), the number of subsets of [s] of size at most k containing no head is at most sum_{j<delta} C(s,j) + 2.3 C(s,k) exp(k(delta-1)/s - k theta/delta). Proof by Lovasz's form of Kruskal-Katona. For the kernel method's dense step at p >= 5 (delta = p-1, s = 15(N+1), k = ceil(sqrt(N Lambda))) it gives a threshold Q_*^(p) = O_p(N^(p-3/2) sqrt(log N)) of distinct heads, against Theta_p(N^(p-1)) possible; at delta = 2 it sharpens (DH-count).

claims.summary: The all-prime graph criterion: for every odd prime p (delta = p-1), a polynomial inventory and sufficiently large N, on the separated sixteen-neighbor graph with s = 15(N+1) projected coordinates, a source of M complete accuracy-one blocks with old inputs of degree at most delta (all companions and coefficient fields) has no ordinary PC refutation through D >= 2p-1 when every block's nonlinear rank r_a in P_{<=delta}/I_delta(Gamma_H) modulo affine is at most R or at least Q_*^(p) = ceil(2^delta delta C(s,delta)((delta-1)/s + 5k/N + (Lambda+1)/k)), with Lambda = log(64(M+1)), k = ceil(sqrt(N Lambda)), T = (p-1)(H_* + delta R) + p and TD + k <= N/10^6 (so RD <= c_p N: R <= N^sigma polylog N for polylog D, R <= c_p N for bounded D). Q_*^(p) = O_p(N^(p-3/2) sqrt(log N)); at p = 3 it is the ternary criterion up to constants.
claims.assessment: Working proof: transcription of the ternary low-or-dense graph criterion, with dense heads taken in the projected coordinates modulo the projected ideal and counted by the bounded-degree head-count lemma, E certified through k+delta-2, beta = f^(p-2) c maps, the all-prime basis conversion and Fermat indicators of degree p-1 on the low side. A fresh-context reviewer found one gap (heads outside the projected coordinates at delta >= 3), repaired. Exact check of the telescoping and product identities modulo Booleanity over F3, F5, F7. Leaves the window R < r_a < Q_*^(p), much wider at p >= 5; not a lower bound for refutations with window blocks.

claims.summary: The all-prime clique-head theorem: under the hypotheses of thm:allprime-low-or-dense-graph-rank-exclusion, blocks satisfying (CH_delta-hyp) for some coordinate set M of size m_*^(p) = ceil((2s/k)(5k^2/N + Lambda + log(C_delta/2))) = O_p(sqrt(N log N)) also join the criterion, where (CH_delta-hyp) asks that every delta-subset of M be a leading monomial of span(inputs) + projected old ideal under the degree-then-M-weight-then-lex order. Lemma CH_delta: a head family containing all delta-subsets of an m-set leaves at most 2 C_delta binom(s,k) exp(-mk/(2s)) sets of size at most k free, with C_delta = (4(delta-1))^(delta-1) e^(1/4-(delta-1)). Random dense blocks with h >= (binom(m,delta) ln p + Lambda)/ln(1/eps_p) inputs satisfy it, eps_p = 1-(1-1/p)^delta, so the threshold for them is Theta_p((N log N)^((p-1)/2)) instead of N^(p-3/2).
claims.assessment: Working proof, transcribing the ternary clique-head refinement; checked by a fresh-context reviewer. The random-block count uses a multilinear Schwartz-Zippel bound and a plain union bound, weaker in constants than the ternary stratified count. The old relations alone cannot satisfy the hypothesis, so a block whose input span has dimension below (2s/k) log(8(M+1)) = O_p(sqrt(N log N)) never does; whether large structured common-factor blocks such as the sunflower family satisfy it is not decided, since their inputs give no coefficient on the relevant delta-subsets but cancellation against the old relations is not excluded. The window stays open at every prime.

claims.summary: Top-size lemma: a normalized mixture of pulled-back restriction designs annihilating U, where all components at sizes outside a set I annihilate U and I meets the nonzero-weight sizes only at the largest one, has a normalized sub-mixture on I annihilating U. Applied, under typicality hypothesis (T), to the ternary endpoint designs and an inventory with n random tuples at every input count: every successful PC mixture contains a degree-D PC design for the old base plus the n tuples of one input count, built from components not required to handle them.
claims.assessment: The lemma is elementary linear algebra with a complete proof; the application is conditional on (T), dense-side rank preservation at every restriction the mixture uses, which has no union bound for families chosen after the inventory. A reduction of the sheaf-entry mixture lead to a one-count design problem, not a refutation of mixtures; the one-count problem is a special case of the window problem and may be easier.

claims.summary: Wide-conditioning conjecture: for each odd p and D there are t,Q such that ordinary unary PHP plus an affine system with linear parts independent modulo rows, every nonzero combination Q-robust on at least t rows, has no degree-D PC refutation. With the transversal special case of the constant-row clamp, a transversal meeting it excludes a compiled source; but any width-t span has dimension at most (N+2-t)(N-1) < N^2, so for about that many random blocks or more no transversal meets the hypothesis. Control: C_j=1 for j<N has width N+1 but a degree-two refutation, so robustness is needed.
claims.assessment: Conjecture, untested beyond its recorded one-form and two-form special cases at their own parameters; the r-parameter lift it needs is unproved and the projective proof does not port. The dimension bound and union bound are proved, and the control is a checked hand refutation. The ceiling limits the conjectured sufficient condition, not transversal or other constant-substitution designs.

formalization.scope: Informal conjecture, counting bound and hand control; no Lean verification.

significance.rationale: States the natural many-form extension of the p-complex lifts; if true it would give quadratic reach for common affine conditioning, beyond the recorded linear endpoints, while its width hypothesis cannot reach polynomially many random window blocks.
significance.next_action: Test the conjecture at constant degree on small robust systems of rank above the one- and two-form cases, or prove an r-parameter lift; it does not by itself address the window.

claims.summary: Row Horace identity: on the functional matching complex, for a row i, K_t = K'_t (+) K^{ni i}_t and D_l = D'_l + partial_l; the double-point space Z = {w in K_3 : D_l^2 w = 0 for all l} equals {w0 + w1 : w1 in Z_res, T w0 = -C w1} with T the trace problem on the board without row i, Z_res = {w1 : D'^2_l w1 = 0} and coupling C = (partial D' + D' partial); so dim Z = dim ker T + dim Z_res - rank(Z_res -> coker T). Each form's gamma_1 - 1 conditions split as (gamma'_1 - 1) + (N - 1). Over F_3, with no form row-constant on the smaller board: if T has maximal rank and Z_res is nondefective, Z has expected dimension when T is onto, and otherwise exactly when the coupling has maximal rank. The identity holds over any field for any forms.

claims.summary: Coupling dual: on the top algebra G of any board over any field, with a row i split G = G' (+) G^{ni i} and forms l = l' + l_i, the double-point multiplication mu: (u_l) -> sum l^2 u_l from (+)G_1 to G_3 has rank = rank mu' + dim(im rho + beta(ker mu')), where mu' is the trace u' -> sum l'^2 u', rho the residual v -> sum l'^2 v on row-i parts, and beta(u') = 2 sum l_i l' u'_l on trace syzygies; if rho is injective, ker mu is isomorphic to {u' in ker mu' : beta(u') in im rho}; in characteristic 3 with every l' nonzero, maximal rank M(gamma_1 - 1) holds exactly when those u' are Frobenius syzygies l' e_l. claims.summary: Quiet members: over F_p, if P in F_p^d is the common zero set of m clauses prod_{j in S_b} L_{b,j}(y)^{p-1} with |S_b|=k <= d affine forms of linearly independent linear parts, then every nonzero reduced polynomial of total degree r vanishing on P satisfies p^{-r/(p-1)} <= m(1-1/p)^k (union bound plus the generalized Reed-Muller minimum weight). At the logarithmic-prefix reduction's parameters (k = ceil((K+1) log n / log(p/(p-1))), at most n^K clauses) m(1-1/p)^k <= 1/n, so a member's local reduction (the functions on its span vanishing on P) has no nonzero element of reduced y-degree below (p-1) log_p n. It bounds y-degree only, over the abstract F_p^d, for clauses of k independent forms.

claims.summary: Pattern row reduction: on the pattern algebra P(R,L) (lex-degenerate functional top algebra, faces of size <= 3 avoiding 0-above-1 and the four triple patterns), characteristic 3, R >= 4, L >= 5, the last-row split P_t = P(R-1,L)_t (+) P^last_t is exact and rank mu = rank mu' + dim(im rho + beta(ker mu')) (coupling-dual formula); the residual splits into label slices y_{R-1,c} V_c with no quotient, dim V_c = C(R-1,2)((L-1)(L-2)-1) (c=0, c>=4), C(R-1,2)(L-2)(L-3) (c=1, the minimum), C(R-1,2)((L-1)(L-2)-2) (c=2), C(R-1,2)((L-1)(L-2)-3) (c=3); by polarization rho is injective for generic forms iff M <= d_1, and ceil(capacity) <= d_1; so maximal rank is equivalent to rank mu' + dim(coupling quotient) = min(gamma_3, M(gamma_1-1)) - ML, checked at M = floor/ceil capacity; the trace capacity is below the total by more than 5, so the coupling is needed; parts 1-3 hold in any characteristic. claims.summary: Kunneth component locality: over F_3, let G be a graded commutative algebra with l^3 = 0 on G_1, and linear forms U = U_1 + ... + U_m whose spans W_i form a direct sum W; with T_i = Sym(W_i)/(cubes), T = Sym(W)/(cubes) = tensor of T_i, A_i = F_3[x_j : j in U_i]/(x_j^3), A = tensor of A_i acting by x_j -> l_j, and any homogeneous J_i in A_i, J = sum J_i A: if G is free through degree B over T (a T-linear map T (x) C -> G bijective in degrees <= B), then Tor_1^A(A/J, G)_s = [sum_i Tor_1^{A_i}(A_i/J_i, T_i) (x) prod_{k != i} T_k/J_k T_k (x) C]_s for s <= B, so every syzygy of the chosen generators of J (the union of generating sets of the J_i) is generated by G-combinations of A-syzygies (Frobenius, Koszul for selectors) and syzygies supported on one component; forms within a component may be dependent. This proves the syzygy conclusion of conj:component-hypothesis for components with independent spans under joint freeness.
claims.assessment: Working proof (truncation, freeness and the Kunneth formula over a field) after a fresh-context review.

significance.rationale: Proves the component hypothesis's syzygy conclusion in the independent-span regime; isolates freeness and span dependence as what remains for adversarial inventories.

claims.summary: Onto stability: over a field of characteristic p, the weak unary base on m rows and N columns together with every column equation sum_i x_ij = 1 (the weak onto system) is refuted at degree 1 if m != N mod p, and otherwise its homogenization is z-injective below D when N >= (p-1)D^2: modulo the column sums the algebra is the weak column tensor power on m-1 rows, whose row-sum syzygies are Frobenius by content reduction and free seeds, and column-sum syzygies are placed (x_ij y e'_j) by Kunneth; all lift. claims.summary: Leaf reduction: over F_3 (also F_q), for a family F of systems (ideals in their private variables and the shared coordinates they read, pairwise disjoint private variables, no cross generators) and a system a reading exactly one shared coordinate x, with U any set of other systems, R = F \ a, and M_U, M_W the top ideals of U and R \ U in the truncated algebra A_R of x and R's variables: if x^alpha A_R cap (M_U + M_W) = (x^alpha A_R cap M_U) + x^alpha M_W for alpha = 1, 2 (a modular law over the chain ring F_3[x]/(x^3); it fails even for ideals, e.g. A_R = S[y]/(y^3), M_U = (x+y), M_W = (y)), then every degree at which F falls (in the family's algebra) is one at which {a} cup U or R falls. Proof: A = A_a tensor_S A_R with an adapted basis for n_a; the law splits N_a cap N_R into N_a cap N_U plus N_a N_W, whose Koszul syzygies lift exactly. Consequence: a path a-b-c-d without cross generators satisfying the law when peeling a (U = {b}) and then b in {b,c,d} (U = {c}) has lowest fall equal to the least over its three linked pairs. Separately, a four-block path of ENS blocks at h = 4 with R on its links (outside the lemma) has no fall below 8 (exact).

claims.summary: Rigid-form reduction: over F_p (p odd), call an affine form L rigid at degree D0 if 1 - L^{p-1} lies in the degree-D0 PC closure of the weak unary base B. With D = (4p-1)(p-1)k: (1) for D0 <= D - (p-1)k, clauses g_i Q_S of rigid excluded forms lie in C_D(B), so the odd-prime wide-clause statement W at degree D is equivalent to W for families whose forms are all non-rigid at degree D0, and a block constrains only when it has more than k non-rigid forms; (2) for D0 <= D - 2(p-1)k, any choice S can be replaced by a non-rigid-first choice S* (keeping S's non-rigid prefix forms) with C_D(B + Cl(S*)) contained in C_D(B + Cl(S)). Padding by base-rigid fillers (2-X_v, C_s-2, R_{n+1}+R_j-1) therefore cannot refute W; forms rigid only modulo other clauses or only above D - (p-1)k, and rarely-zero non-rigid forms, are not removed.

claims.summary: Occupancy-pinned PHP (conjecture): over F_3 there are c > 0 and, for each n, some e <= n/2 with e = 2 (mod 3) such that weak unary PHP^{n+1}_n plus the pins C_j = 0 (j <= e) and C_j = 1 (j > e) has no PC refutation of degree n^c. The pinned system is an onto weak PHP (rows sum to 1 mod 3, each remaining hole exactly one pigeon) of n+1 pigeons into n-e holes with counts agreeing mod 3; e not = 2 (mod 3) is refuted at degree 1 by counting. It is implied by a PC lower bound for Beame-Riis onto functional PHP^{N+3^l}_N over F_3 (listed open in their 1998 paper), and it transfers their Nullstellensatz bound: NS coefficient degree >= 2l-1 (about 1.37 log_3 n, a constant factor below the needed 4(K+1) log_3 n) when e+1 = 3^l and n-e >= (5^l - 3^l)/2; their Lemma 8.7 refutes their system at NS degree 3^l - 1, so this route needs e+1 = 3^l above the target degree. The reduction needs only degree O(log n); n^c is a stronger form. Mikša-Nordström's onto PHP (pigeon clauses) does not cover the mod-3 linear rows.
claims.assessment: Proved for n >= 5 with e = 2 and c = 1/3 by cor:column-statistic-families-random-prefix (restriction to onto weak PHP and thm:spare-pigeon-onto-hardness); degree bound ceil((n-2)/2)+1.

claims.summary: Subflat obstruction: over F_p, p odd, replace each Res(Lin_Fp) line's falsifying set {f_i != a_i} by kept value sets {f_i in T_i}, T_i a nonempty subset of F_p minus a_i. claims.summary: Bit block over the weak base: over F_3, for the standard bit-encoding block, one block of the (n+1)beta forms L_{i,b} = sum_{j in J_b} x_ij (J_b the holes whose binary code has bit b, beta = ceil(log_2 n)), and n with n' >= 1 (n >= 2 l beta^2 suffices), weak PHP^{n+1}_n plus the pins L_{i,b} = q_{i,b}, for any q with the top-bit values 0, has no PC refutation of degree <= ceil(n'/2), where n' >= n/(l beta^2) - 1 and l is the least integer with (2/3)^{l-1} beta < 1: groups of l disjoint radius-1 Hamming stars in the lower cube are additive bases of F_3^beta (Alon-Linial-Meshulam Proposition 3.1) and serve as super-holes in lem:super-hole-substitution. claims.summary: Covering identity: over F_3 on the weak base, for a block with affine forms L_1..L_h, g_u = 1 - L_u^2, prefix C in F_3^{t x h}, Q^C = prod_j (1 - s_j^2) with s = C g, and G = prod_u L_u^2 (no form vanishes), Q^C = G + sum_u prod_{u'<u}(1 - g_{u'}) g_u Q^C modulo the base, all products of unreduced degree <= 2h + 4t (g^2 = g at degree 4 from L^3 = L by Frobenius; s_j G = 0; telescoping 1 - G); so for D >= 2h + 4t the degree-D closures of the base plus Q^C and of the base plus the W_RS clauses g_u Q^C plus the covering axiom G coincide. claims.summary: Pattern-poor support: over F_3, if weak unary PHP^{n+1}_n has a degree-D Nullstellensatz design sum_{x in X} a_x ev_x with X fixed before the prefixes, and P_b(X) is the set of nonzero zero patterns g_b(x) of block b on X (blocks fixed in advance), then for uniform C_b in F_3^{t x h_b}, with probability >= 1 - 3^{-t} sum_b |P_b(X)| every randomized-prefix clause vanishes on X and the design survives, so weak PHP plus all clauses has no Nullstellensatz refutation of degree D (trivial unless 4t+2 <= D). The W_RS analogue of the main record's pointwise-lift support union bound, counting zero patterns instead of points; relaxes prop:bounded-column-vacuity. claims.summary: Degree-two pin reduction (a sufficient condition): over any field, n >= 3, for FPHP^m_n plus affine pins L_k = l_k + c_k = q_k, if (i) the linear parts l_k are independent modulo row sums and (ii) the multiplication map V^h -> R_2, (lambda_k) -> sum lambda_k l_k, has only Koszul kernel, where V is the cell space modulo row sums and R_2 is the direct sum over pairs of rows of zero-diagonal n x n matrices modulo row and column sums (dim R_2 = C(m,2)(n^2-3n+1)), then there is no Nullstellensatz refutation of degree 2. The affine degree-2 consequences of the rows are only their span (one relation per pair of rows, n >= 3). Condition (ii) needs hm(n-1) - C(h,2) <= dim R_2, a margin D_1 - h below the model's fill point, so the lemma is sufficient, not necessary; (ii) itself is open.
claims.assessment: Working proof of the sufficient condition, after a fresh-context review; condition (ii) for generic or random pins at every n is open (the recorded series at n = 7..10 is consistent with it but does not imply it).
